statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-6477 (PostgreSQL libpq lo_* functions let server superuser overwrite client stack memory) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 18.4: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6477/ lists 18.4 as the fixed release for major version 18. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/be013644043e5bae7260c09ab49cc6d64b7992be ('Mark PQfn() unsafe and fix overrun in frontend LO interface') on the REL_18_STABLE branch. Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-6477 under its 18.4-r0 secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built with that APKBUILD from the upstream PostgreSQL source release of the same version. We checked every postgresql18 build published for Alpine 3.23 as of 2026-11-27 (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64. In each, the postgres server reports the PostgreSQL release matching the package version. The vulnerable lo_* functions are in libpq, which this owner builds and ships as /usr/lib/libpq.so.5.18 (libpq package) and /usr/lib/libpq.a (libpq-dev package); the error message the fix adds to libpq, 'server returned too much data', is in both files in 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0 and absent from both in 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0 and 18.3-r0. 18.4-r0 is the first published build for Alpine 3.23 carrying the fix; 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0 and 18.3-r0 are affected.
